name: drought-window-class-crossing
definition: GDACS's currently-OPEN drought episodes fall into two classes established by obs-2026-08-10-1.json and confirmed stable across six recorded nights by obs-2026-08-15-1.json: 'rolling' (properties.todate sits at exactly run_date minus 2 calendar days on every observation, advancing by the real number of elapsed calendar days even across gaps in this observatory's own run cadence -- gdacs-dr-1018332, gdacs-dr-1018431, gdacs-dr-1027450, gdacs-dr-1027465) and 'frozen' (properties.todate byte-identical across every preserved snapshot -- gdacs-dr-1017863, gdacs-dr-1018327). No drought has crossed between classes and no new drought has entered the registry since 2026-08-08. This sensor watches for the crossing the two-night predecessor observation could not yet rule out: a rolling drought's todate stopping (GDACS deciding to stop actively updating an episode it was tracking daily) or a frozen drought's todate resuming motion (GDACS returning to an episode it had stopped touching).
test_rule: On each nightly run, after gdacs_futures() extracts the night's drought features, for every OPEN drought future with at least two prior preserved GDACS snapshots: compute delta_days = (run_date - todate). Classify as rolling if delta_days has equalled the number of calendar days since the future's earliest preserved observation at every check so far (i.e. todate has advanced by exactly one calendar day per calendar day elapsed, with no exceptions), frozen if todate has been byte-identical across at least two consecutive preserved snapshots. A future already classified rolling that shows todate NOT advance this run (delta_days grew by more than the calendar days elapsed since the last run) is a rolling-to-frozen crossing. A future already classified frozen that shows todate change at all is a frozen-to-rolling crossing. Record {future_id, from_class, to_class, run_date} in that night's run summary the first time either happens. The sensor fires on any non-empty crossing list -- a single crossing is itself the finding, no threshold or baseline needed, the same shape as sensor-primary-iso3-gap's unconditional fire rule.
falsification: Falsified as a meaningful distinction, not merely as an empty sensor, if a crossing turns out to correlate with nothing about the episode itself -- e.g. if GDACS's daily job that keeps the rolling class moving (identified in obs-2026-08-15-1.json as a fixed ~05:57 UTC daily stamp) is later found to be an artefact of GDACS's own feed-generation infrastructure unrelated to the episode's real status (for instance, a scheduled job that touches every drought episode below some ID cutoff regardless of activity) -- at that point 'rolling' would mean 'old enough to be in the job's scope', not 'actively monitored', and the sensor's crossing alert would need to be read very differently, or dropped. Also falsified if no crossing occurs for a very long time purely because these six specific episodes are unusually stable -- the sensor would then only ever prove itself against six examples and should not be generalised to GDACS's other hazard types (flood, earthquake, wildfire, tropical cyclone) without separately checking whether their window.to fields show the same two-class split, which this proposal has not checked.

implementation.how: drought_window_class(future, day) reconstructs the whole window.to trajectory from the future's own committed history alone -- window is already a TRACKED_FIELD, so every change GDACS's todate ever carried is already an appended REVISED event; no state beyond the registry, no re-reading of raw snapshot files. A night with no REVISED window event still counts as an observation: the classifier carries the last known value forward to tonight's date before checking the calendar-day-per-calendar-day rule, so a rolling drought that stops advancing shows up as a broken step the night it happens rather than as silence. drought_window_crossings(registry, day) recomputes yesterday's classification by re-running the same function against the future's history with tonight's own events stripped out -- stateless by construction, matching I3 (no stored prior state to drift from the record). run.py records drought_window_class per OPEN drought and drought_window_crossings under new run.json fields, additive, alongside overdue_cold_start/overdue_drift's own pattern.
implementation.refined_from_proposal: The proposal's own test_rule named two directions of crossing (rolling-to-frozen, frozen-to-rolling) as a binary split. The implementation adds a third class, irregular, for any step that does not match either clean pattern exactly (a day_delta that does not equal the todate_delta) -- a strictly more cautious generalisation, since a rolling drought's first stalled night lands in irregular rather than being force-fitted into 'frozen' before enough nights exist to say so. A transition into or out of irregular is itself recorded as a crossing (any today_state != prior_state), so the proposal's own fire condition -- any non-empty crossing list -- is unchanged in effect.
implementation.practice/tests/test_foreknown.py: test_drought_window_class_needs_two_nights_before_deciding, test_drought_window_class_frozen_when_window_to_never_changes, test_drought_window_class_rolling_when_window_to_advances_a_day_a_night, test_drought_window_class_flags_a_stalled_rolling_drought_as_irregular, test_drought_window_class_ignores_non_drought_and_closed_futures, test_drought_window_crossings_catches_a_rolling_drought_that_stalls -- the last constructs a rolling history then checks one night past its last recorded change and confirms both the irregular classification and the crossing record the falsification-worried scenario (a rolling drought's todate stopping) actually produces.

promotion.settles: the proposal's test_rule, applied nightly since 2026-08-08 (via manual re-derivation from preserved snapshots each of the two prior observations) and now against tonight's committed registry: 9 nights (2026-08-08 through 2026-08-17) show the same clean two-class split with zero crossings -- four rolling droughts (gdacs-dr-1018332, gdacs-dr-1018431, gdacs-dr-1027450, gdacs-dr-1027465), two frozen (gdacs-dr-1017863, gdacs-dr-1018327).
promotion.why_promoted_before_a_crossing_happened: sensor-primary-iso3-gap.json set the precedent: a sensor whose expected value is quiet is promotable once the code exists to turn a future crossing into a visible row instead of a silence, not only after it fires once. This proposal's own test_rule needs no threshold or baseline -- any crossing is itself the finding -- so there is nothing further to calibrate by waiting.
promotion.falsification_clause_checked_tonight: the proposal's own first falsification risk -- 'a scheduled job that touches every drought episode below some ID cutoff regardless of activity' -- was directly tested tonight rather than assumed away: obs-2026-08-17-1.json found exactly this batch-artefact failure mode in a *different* GDACS field (properties.datemodified, 19 of 95 open futures across four hazard types sharing one of two exact-millisecond 2026-02-11 timestamps) and, in the same check, confirmed properties.todate does not show it -- only the four already-tracked rolling droughts, no other hazard type, carry todate == run_date-2 tonight. The two frozen droughts sit in the same hazard category as the rolling four and are untouched, which a hazard-wide or ID-range batch job could not produce. The clause's second risk (six examples being unusually stable, not generalisable to other hazard types) is unaffected by promotion: the code is scoped to hazard=='drought' exactly as GDACS reports it, the same scoping sensor-primary-iso3-gap.json and sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot.json already apply to other GDACS-only fields, and extending it to other hazard types remains a separate, unproposed decision.
